claims.evidence: This claim is supported by cryoEM 2D class averages shown in Figure 2b and c.

claims.claim: In the isNS1wt:Fab56.2 ternary complex dataset, two apparent but rare sub-classes of free sNS1wt dimer bound to two units of Fab56.2 representing 3.5% of the total population of picked particles were observed.
claims.source: In the isNS1wt:Fab56.2 ternary complex dataset, we further observed two apparent but rare sub-classes of free sNS1wt dimer bound to two units of Fab56.2 representing 3.5% of the total population of picked particles (Figure 2c, red dashed boxes).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by cryoEM data shown in Figure 2c.

claims.claim: The AlphaFold2 predicted model of the NS1 dimer and Fab models fitted into the cryoEM map with a correlation value of 0.75 to the fitted regions using a simulated 5 Å map.
claims.source: While the cryoEM map reconstructions remain limited at low resolutions (Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2), they could be fitted with the NS1 dimer and Fab56.2 models (Figure 2d) predicted separately using AlphaFold2 (Jumper et al., 2021; Mirdita et al., 2022), with a correlation value of 0.75 to the fitted regions using a simulated 5 Å map from the NS1 dimer and Fab models.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by model fitting to cryoEM data shown in Figure 2d.

claims.claim: The approximate dimensions of the spherical HDL could be measured at 82 Å by 65 Å.
claims.source: The approximate dimensions of the spherical HDL could also be measured at 82 Å by 65 Å (Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2), which aligned with existing reports of spherical HDL being measured at 70–120 Å in diameter with predominantly homodimeric ApoA1 arranged as an anti-parallel double-belt stabilized by intermolecular salt bridges (Silva et al., 2008; He et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by cryoEM measurements shown in supplementary figures and citations to previous HDL structural studies.

claims.claim: The NS1 dimer appears semi-embedded on the HDL particle through its hydrophobic surface, with a conformation that exposed only one end of the β-ladder domain to which Ab56.2 and Fab56.2 bind.
claims.source: The NS1 dimer appears semi-embedded on the HDL particle through its hydrophobic surface, with a conformation that exposed only one end of the β-ladder domain to which Ab56.2 and Fab56.2 bind.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on interpretation of the cryoEM structural model.

claims.claim: 2D class averages of isNS1ts:Fab56.2 dataset showed a significant sub-population of a free NS1ts dimer bound to two units of Fab56.2 (53.7%), in addition to the HDL spheres (23.6%) and isNS1ts dimer:HDL:Fab56.2 (22.7%) classes.
claims.source: Interestingly, 2D class averages of isNS1ts:Fab56.2 dataset showed a significant sub-population of a free NS1ts dimer bound to two units of Fab56.2 (53.7%), in addition to the HDL spheres (23.6%) and isNS1ts dimer:HDL:Fab56.2 (22.7%) classes (Figure 3b, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by cryoEM 2D classification data shown in Figure 3b.

claims.claim: A comparison of the cryoEM density maps of free isNS1ts dimer:Fab56.2 and isNS1ts dimer:HDL:Fab56.2 ternary complex revealed a pose difference of the Fab56.2 between the free isNS1ts dimer and the HDL-bound isNS1ts dimer.
claims.source: A comparison of the cryoEM density maps of free isNS1ts dimer:Fab56.2 (Figure 3D, gray) and isNS1ts dimer:HDL:Fab56.2 ternary complex (Figure 3d, yellow) fitted with a correlation value of 0.71 based on the NS1 map region revealed a pose difference of the Fab56.2 between the free isNS1ts dimer and the HDL-bound isNS1ts dimer (Figure 3d, inset).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of cryoEM maps shown in Figure 3d.

claims.claim: Comparison of the density maps of the isNS1 dimer:HDL population in the Fab56.2 ternary complexes of isNS1wt and isNS1ts revealed conformational similarities of the isNS1 dimer:HDL complex.
claims.source: Further comparison of the density maps of the isNS1 dimer:HDL population in the Fab56.2 ternary complexes of isNS1wt (Figure 3e, purple) and isNS1ts (Figure 3e, yellow) revealed conformational similarities of the isNS1 dimer:HDL complex.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of cryoEM maps shown in Figure 3e.

claims.claim: 28 NS1:NS1 and 29 ApoA1:ApoA1 intramolecular crosslinks, as well as 25 NS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks were identified for isNS1wt.
claims.source: We identified 28 NS1:NS1 and 29 ApoA1:ApoA1 intramolecular crosslinks, as well as 25 NS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks for isNS1wt (Figure 4b; Supplementary file 2 and 3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4b and supplementary files.

claims.claim: The NS1 residues that are involved in both intra- and intermolecular crosslinks were located mainly on the β-roll and wing domains, with ~34% of the NS1:ApoA1 crosslinks being located on the β-roll domain.
claims.source: As depicted in Figure 4b and c, the NS1 residues that are involved in both intra- and intermolecular crosslinks were located mainly on the β-roll and wing domains, with ~34% of the NS1:ApoA1 crosslinks being located on the β-roll domain.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4b and c.

claims.claim: 85% of the NS1:NS1 intramolecular crosslinks (24 out of 28) met the 30 Å cutoff distance criterion for the Cα atoms of crosslinked residues on the predicted NS1 dimer model.
claims.source: The NS1:NS1 intramolecular crosslink pairs were further validated on the predicted NS1 dimer model by implementing a 30 Å cutoff distance for the Cα atoms of crosslinked residues, a criterion that was met by 85% of the NS1:NS1 intramolecular crosslinks (24 out of 28; Figure 4d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by validation of crosslinking data against the structural model shown in Figure 4d.

claims.claim: The NS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks for the immunoaffinity-purified isNS1wt were found to be located between the β-roll and wing domains of NS1 and the helices 3, 4, 8, and 10 of ApoA1.
claims.source: The NS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks for the immunoaffinity-purified isNS1wt were found to be located between the β-roll and wing domains of NS1 and the helices 3, 4, 8, and 10 of ApoA1 (Figure 4b and d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4b and d.

claims.claim: 76% of the NS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks (19 out of 25) satisfied the <30 Å distance between their Cα atoms cutoff when validated on the cryoEM model of isNS1wt.
claims.source: Applying the same cutoff value of <30 Å distance between the Cα atoms of the NS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinked residues and validating it on the cryoEM model of isNS1wt in this study (Figure 4d and e) satisfied 76% of the crosslinks (19 out of 25 intermolecular crosslinks between NS1 dimer and ApoA1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by validation of crosslinking data against the cryoEM model shown in Figure 4d and e.

claims.claim: 62% of the ApoA1:ApoA1 intramolecular crosslinks (18 out of 29) satisfied the <30 Å distance between their Cα atoms cutoff.
claims.source: In the case of ApoA1:ApoA1 intramolecular crosslinks, the <30 Å distance between their Cα atoms cutoff satisfied 62% of the crosslinks (18 out of 29 ApoA1:ApoA1 intramolecular crosslinks).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by validation of crosslinking data against the structural model.

claims.claim: The higher number of violated crosslinks in ApoA1:ApoA1 compared to those in NS1:NS1 could be due to the flexible and dynamic nature of ApoA1 dimers.
claims.source: The higher number of violated crosslinks in ApoA1:ApoA1 compared to those in NS1:NS1 could be due to the flexible and dynamic nature of ApoA1 dimers, which may prevent it from assuming a fixed relative position among the ApoA1 dimer population in the HDL.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation/speculation based on the crosslinking data and known properties of ApoA1.

claims.claim: isNS1ts dimer may have a weaker affinity to HDL in comparison to the isNS1wt dimer.
claims.source: This indicated that isNS1ts dimer may have a weaker affinity to HDL in comparison to the isNS1wt dimer.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of fewer crosslink sites in isNS1ts and the presence of free isNS1ts dimers in cryoEM data.

claims.claim: The crosslinked rsNS1 alone appeared as higher oligomer bands of dimers, tetramers, and hexamers on the SDS-PAGE analysis.
claims.source: The crosslinked rsNS1 alone appeared as higher oligomer bands of dimers, tetramers, and hexamers on the SDS-PAGE analysis (Figure 4f, lane 3, Figure 4—source data 2), which differed from the crosslinked isNS1 (Figure 4a, lane 3).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by SDS-PAGE data shown in Figure 4f.

claims.claim: The addition of human HDL and crosslinker to rsNS1 resulted in a smearing band ranging from 30 to 150 kDa with the loss of the well-defined monomeric rsNS1 band.
claims.source: Interestingly, the addition of human HDL and crosslinker resulted in a smearing band ranging from 30 to 150 kDa with the loss of the well-defined monomeric rsNS1 band (Figure 4f, lane 4).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by SDS-PAGE data shown in Figure 4f.

claims.claim: In the crosslinked rsNS1 in the absence of HDL, 17 NS1:NS1 intramolecular crosslinks at the β-roll and wing domains were identified.
claims.source: In the crosslinked rsNS1 in the absence of HDL, we identified 17 NS1:NS1 intramolecular crosslinks at the β-roll and wing domains (Figure 4f and g, Supplementary file 4 and 5).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4f and g.

claims.claim: In the presence of human HDL, 30 ApoA1:ApoA1, 4 NS1:NS1, and 6 NS1:ApoA1 crosslinks were identified in rsNS1 samples.
claims.source: In the presence of human HDL, we identified 30 ApoA1:ApoA1, 4 NS1:NS1, and 6 NS1:ApoA1 crosslinks (Supplementary file 4 and 5).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by crosslinking mass spectrometry data in supplementary files.

claims.claim: Only one out of six rsNS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks was within the 30 Å cutoff distance when mapped to the NS1:ApoA1 cryoEM model.
claims.source: Only one out of six rsNS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks was within the 30 Å cutoff distance when mapped to the NS1:ApoA1 cryoEM model (Figure 4e).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by validation of crosslinking data against the cryoEM model.

claims.claim: rsNS1 may form oligomers of dimers but not a complex with HDL under the tested conditions.
claims.source: Overall, this suggests that rsNS1 may form oligomers of dimers but not a complex with HDL under the tested conditions.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the crosslinking mass spectrometry data comparing rsNS1 with and without HDL.

claims.claim: The greatest competition in the NS1 peptide competition ELISA was observed at the NS1 peptide spanning residues 316–330 out of 301–340.
claims.source: The greatest competition was observed at the NS1 peptide spanning residues 316–330 out of 301–340 which showed a decrease in OD450 absorbance (Figure 5b).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by peptide competition ELISA data shown in Figure 5b.

claims.claim: Comparative HDX results revealed global-scale protection against deuterium exchange of rsNS1c in the presence of Fab56.2.
claims.source: Comparative HDX results revealed global-scale protection against deuterium exchange of rsNS1c in the presence of Fab56.2 (Figure 6a, Figure 6—figure supplement 1a), indicative of reduced conformational dynamics.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 6a.

claims.claim: Large-scale differences in deuterium exchange were primarily observed across peptides spanning the dimer interface (residues 174–186) and at the tip of the C-terminal β-ladder (residues 286–347) of rsNS1c.
claims.source: Large-scale differences in deuterium exchange were primarily observed across peptides spanning the dimer interface (residues 174–186) and at the tip of the C-terminal β-ladder (residues 286–347) of rsNS1c (Figure 6b).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 6b.

claims.claim: Multiple overlapping peptides, spanning residues 286–347, showed protection against deuterium exchange even at the longer labeling times (100 min) in rsNS1c:Fab56.2 complex.
claims.source: Multiple overlapping peptides, spanning residues 286–347 (Figure 6b), showed protection against deuterium exchange even at the longer labeling times (100 min) in rsNS1c:Fab56.2 complex (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a, Supplementary file 6).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 6b and supplementary data.

claims.claim: rsNS1c binds stably to Fab56.2 at the primary epitope site of residues 300–310.
claims.source: Coupled with the observation that the most significant change in the differential plot was at residues 300–310 (Figure 6a), these results collectively indicate that rsNS1c binds stably to Fab56.2 at the primary epitope site of residues 300–310.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on HDX-MS data shown in Figure 6a and other supporting data.

claims.claim: Comparative HDX results of rsNS1c-bound and free Fab56.2 revealed protection against deuterium exchange of all three complementarity-determining regions (CDR) of the heavy chain and CDRL2 of the light chain.
claims.source: Comparative HDX results of rsNS1c-bound and free Fab56.2 revealed protection against deuterium exchange of all three complementarity-determining regions (CDR) of the heavy chain (Figure 6c, Figure 6—figure supplement 1b) and CDRL2 of the light chain (Figure 6d, Figure 6—figure supplement 1c).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS data shown in Figure 6c and d.

claims.claim: Peptides spanning CDRH3 (residues 89–116) showed the largest magnitude decrease in deuterium exchange at all labeling time points upon binding to rsNS1c.
claims.source: Upon binding to rsNS1c, peptides spanning CDRH3 (residues 89–116) showed the largest magnitude decrease in deuterium exchange at all labeling time points, while CDRH2 showed minor significant differences.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS data.

claims.claim: Only the CDRL2 loop (residues 49–56) of the light chain of Fab56.2 showed significantly decreased deuterium exchange upon binding to rsNS1c.
claims.source: In addition, only the CDRL2 loop (residues 49–56) of the light chain of Fab56.2 showed significantly decreased deuterium exchange.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by HDX-MS data.

claims.claim: CDRH1-3 and CDRL2 loops were spatially co-localized to form the paratope site to bind rsNS1c, with the heavy chain being the primary anchor.
claims.source: Mapping of the deuterium exchange profiles of heavy and light chains onto a model of Fab56.2 (Figure 6e) revealed that CDRH1-3 and CDRL2 loops were spatially co-localized to form the paratope site to bind rsNS1c, with the heavy chain being the primary anchor.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on HDX-MS data mapped onto the Fab56.2 model shown in Figure 6e.

claims.claim: The mouse sera immunoaffinity purified sNS1ts was detected at ~250 kDa by both anti-ApoA1 and anti-NS1 antibodies in a western blot analysis following separation on a Native-PAGE.
claims.source: The mouse sera immunoaffinity purified sNS1ts was detected at ~250 kDa by both anti-ApoA1 and anti-NS1 antibodies in a western blot analysis following separation on a Native-PAGE (Figure 7a, Figure 7—source data 1), supporting our mass spectrometry finding that ApoA1 is part of the ~250 kDa isNS1 protein complex purified from infected Vero cells (Figure 1d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data from mouse sera shown in Figure 7a.

claims.claim: Increasing the anti-ApoA1 antibody from 10 to 50 µg coupled onto Protein AG resin for pull-down resulted in a corresponding increase in the sNS1 amount detected by ELISA in human patient serum.
claims.source: Increasing the anti-ApoA1 antibody from 10 to 50 µg coupled onto Protein AG resin for pull-down resulted in a corresponding increase in the sNS1 amount detected by ELISA (Figure 7b), suggesting a specific association between sNS1 and ApoA1.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunoprecipitation and ELISA data from human patient serum shown in Figure 7b.

claims.claim: NS1 interacts with HDL regardless of the source of mammalian ApoA1.
claims.source: The observation that NS1 interacts with HDL regardless of the source of mammalian ApoA1 is unsurprising, given the high sequence similarity of bovine and mouse HDL to human HDL of approximately 79 and 65%, respectively (Figure 7, Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and that the structure of ApoA1 is highly conserved (Malajczuk et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on sequence similarity data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and citation to structural conservation.

claims.claim: Bovine HDL has approximately 79% sequence similarity to human HDL.
claims.source: The observation that NS1 interacts with HDL regardless of the source of mammalian ApoA1 is unsurprising, given the high sequence similarity of bovine and mouse HDL to human HDL of approximately 79 and 65%, respectively (Figure 7, Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and that the structure of ApoA1 is highly conserved (Malajczuk et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Mouse HDL has approximately 65% sequence similarity to human HDL.
claims.source: The observation that NS1 interacts with HDL regardless of the source of mammalian ApoA1 is unsurprising, given the high sequence similarity of bovine and mouse HDL to human HDL of approximately 79 and 65%, respectively (Figure 7, Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and that the structure of ApoA1 is highly conserved (Malajczuk et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The structure of ApoA1 is highly conserved.
claims.source: The observation that NS1 interacts with HDL regardless of the source of mammalian ApoA1 is unsurprising, given the high sequence similarity of bovine and mouse HDL to human HDL of approximately 79 and 65%, respectively (Figure 7, Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and that the structure of ApoA1 is highly conserved (Malajczuk et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claims.claim: The data points to the association of ApoA1 with sNS1 in vivo.
claims.source: Collectively, despite the limited amount of sNS1 in sera samples from DENV-infected mice or humans, our data points to the association of ApoA1 with sNS1 in vivo.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data from mouse and human sera.

claims.claim: Benfrid et al. (2022) reconstituted complexes of rsNS1 dimers bound to the surface of a spheroid human HDL particle in vitro at 1:1 to 3:1 ratio when up to 400 μg/mL of rsNS1 were used.
claims.source: Benfrid et al. (2022) recently reconstituted complexes of rsNS1 dimers bound to the surface of a spheroid human HDL particle in vitro at 1:1 to 3:1 ratio when up to 400 μg/mL of rsNS1 were used Benfrid et al., 2022.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to recent research.

claims.claim: Up to two NS1 dimers docked onto an HDL particle were observed in studies with infection-derived sNS1 (isNS1).
claims.source: Similarly, in our studies with infection-derived sNS1 (isNS1), we observed up to two NS1 dimers docked onto an HDL particle (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c, Figures 2 and 3, Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by cryoEM data shown in multiple figures.

claims.claim: The concentration of isNS1:HDL in the study (~30 μg/mL) is closer to the maximum clinically reported concentration of sNS1 in the sera of DENV patients (50 μg/mL).
claims.source: It is noteworthy that the concentration of isNS1:HDL in our study (~30 μg/mL) is closer to the maximum clinically reported concentration of sNS1 in the sera of DENV patients (50 μg/mL) Libraty et al., 2002; Young et al., 2000; Alcon et al., 2002.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on comparison with clinically reported concentrations cited from previous studies.

claims.claim: The ratio of sNS1 to HDL varies depending on the concentration of the proteins used for complex formation.
claims.source: Therefore, the ratio of sNS1 to HDL varies depending on the concentration of the proteins used for complex formation.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of different experimental conditions.

claims.claim: The data does not support the widely held view that sNS1 is composed of a trimer of NS1 dimers with an ~28 Å wide central channel filled with lipid.
claims.source: While our study is limited to only one antibody (56.2) for immunoaffinity purification, our key take-home message in terms of structure is that our data does not support the widely held view that sNS1 is composed of a trimer of NS1 dimers with an ~28 Å wide central channel filled with lipid as established in several seminal publications (Flamand et al., 1999; Gutsche et al., 2011; Muller et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion based on the structural data from this study compared to previous models.

claims.claim: The data confirms the observations reported in Benfrid et al., 2022.
claims.source: In fact, our data confirms the observations reported in Benfrid et al., 2022.
claims.evidence: This is a statement comparing the current findings with previous research.

claims.claim: In the rare instances where trimer of dimers have been experimentally shown by cryoEM of rNS1 structures, only a single lipid molecule can be found in the narrow central channel.
claims.source: In the rare instances where trimer of dimers have been experimentally shown by cryoEM of rNS1 structures (Shu et al., 2022), only a single lipid molecule can be found in the narrow central channel and unlikely to be reflective of sNS1 circulating in serum.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on citation to previous cryoEM studies and interpretation of their findings.

claims.claim: The amount of lipid associated with infection-derived sNS1 is consistent with NS1 dimer(s) associated with HDL.
claims.source: We argue that the amount of lipid associated with infection-derived sNS1 (Gutsche et al., 2011; Chan et al., 2019) is consistent with NS1 dimer(s) associated with HDL.
claims.evidence: This is an argument based on comparison of lipid content data from previous studies with the current structural model.

claims.claim: The interaction with HDL requires an exposed hydrophobic face of NS1 that is incompatible to the hexamer model of sNS1.
claims.source: The interaction with HDL requires an exposed hydrophobic face of NS1 that is incompatible to the hexamer model of sNS1.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the structural requirements for NS1-HDL interaction.

claims.claim: The oligomeric state of NS1 is dynamic, which may vary depending on the context and environment.
claims.source: Indeed, it is agreeable that the oligomeric state of NS1 is dynamic, which may vary depending on the context and environment.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement acknowledging the complexity of NS1 oligomerization.

claims.claim: Incubating immunoaffinity-purified sNS1 with human PBMCs from three independent human donors triggered the production of proinflammatory cytokines IL6 and TNFα in a concentration-dependent manner.
claims.source: Our previous functional studies comparing isNS1wt with isNS1ts (T164S) showed that incubating immunoaffinity-purified sNS1 with human PBMCs from three independent human donors triggered the production of proinflammatory cytokines IL6 and TNFα in a concentration-dependent manner and that it was more pronounced with the mutant than the WT (Chan et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous functional studies by the authors.

claims.claim: The proinflammatory cytokine production was more pronounced with the isNS1ts mutant than the WT.
claims.source: Our previous functional studies comparing isNS1wt with isNS1ts (T164S) showed that incubating immunoaffinity-purified sNS1 with human PBMCs from three independent human donors triggered the production of proinflammatory cytokines IL6 and TNFα in a concentration-dependent manner and that it was more pronounced with the mutant than the WT (Chan et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous functional studies by the authors.

claims.claim: Acid-eluted isNS1 proteins in this study induce endothelial hyperpermeability.
claims.source: Furthermore, we have provisional transendothelial electrical resistance (TEER) assay data with isNS1 proteins used in the structural studies with human umbilical vascular endothelial cells (hUVEC), which show that acid-eluted isNS1 proteins in this study induces endothelial hyperpermeability as shown in previous studies (Puerta-Guardo et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is based on provisional TEER assay data and citation to previous studies.

claims.claim: The presence of a significant population of free isNS1ts dimers in complex with Fab56.2 and fewer crosslinks identified between isNS1ts and ApoA1 point toward the possibility that isNS1ts is more dynamic in its association with host proteins than isNS1wt.
claims.source: The presence of a significant population of free isNS1ts dimers in complex with Fab56.2 and fewer crosslinks identified between isNS1ts and ApoA1 point toward the possibility that isNS1ts is more dynamic in its association with host proteins than isNS1wt.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on cryoEM and crosslinking data comparing isNS1wt and isNS1ts.

claims.claim: The disease severity and increased complement protein expression in AG129 mice liver infected with NS1T164S carrying virus compared with WT can be ascribed to weakly bound mutant NS1 with fast on/off rate with HDL being transported to the liver where specific receptors bind to free sNS1 and interact with effector proteins such as complement to drive inflammation and associated pathology.
claims.source: The disease severity and increased complement protein expression in AG129 mice liver infected with NS1T164S carrying virus compared with WT that was observed in our previous study (Chan et al., 2019) can be ascribed to weakly bound mutant NS1 with fast on/off rate with HDL being transported to the liver where specific receptors bind to free sNS1 and interact with effector proteins such as complement to drive inflammation and associated pathology.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative mechanistic explanation based on previous in vivo data and the current structural findings.

claims.claim: Contrary to the known protective roles of HDL, sNS1:HDL complex triggers proinflammatory signals when tested with primary human macrophages.
claims.source: Contrary to the known protective roles of HDL such as against endotoxic shock caused by lipopolysaccharides (Trinder et al., 2020; Tall, 2021; Harsløf et al., 2023), Benfrid et al. (2022) showed that sNS1:HDL complex triggers proinflammatory signals when tested with primary human macrophages (Benfrid et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on HDL protective roles and sNS1:HDL complex effects.

claims.claim: The presence of sNS1:HDL complexes as a predominant population of sNS1 in the in vitro infection model corroborates with a previous report of an interaction between insect-derived recombinant NS1 and the classical HDL/ApoA1-binding receptor known as SR-BI.
claims.source: The presence of sNS1:HDL complexes as a predominant population of sNS1 in our in vitro infection model corroborates with a previous report of an interaction between insect-derived recombinant NS1 and the classical HDL/ApoA1-binding receptor known as SR-BI (Alcalá et al., 2022), which is primarily expressed on hepatocytes (Acton et al., 1996).
claims.evidence: This claim connects the current findings with previous research through citations.

claims.claim: SR-BI is primarily expressed on hepatocytes.
claims.source: The presence of sNS1:HDL complexes as a predominant population of sNS1 in our in vitro infection model corroborates with a previous report of an interaction between insect-derived recombinant NS1 and the classical HDL/ApoA1-binding receptor known as SR-BI (Alcalá et al., 2022), which is primarily expressed on hepatocytes (Acton et al., 1996).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: The interaction with SR-BI in hepatocytes has been suggested to trigger endocytosis of sNS1 and subsequent downstream effects including vascular permeability.
claims.source: This interaction in hepatocytes has been suggested to trigger endocytosis of sNS1 and subsequent downstream effects including vascular permeability, which is a characteristic feature of severe dengue (Alcalá et al., 2022; Alcon-LePoder et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claims.claim: Internalization of sNS1 is critical for increased virus production in hepatocytes.
claims.source: Internalization of sNS1 is critical for increased virus production in hepatocytes (Alcon-LePoder et al., 2005) and NS1-mediated permeability in endothelial cells (Wang et al., 2019).

results.result: The major species of infection-derived sNS1 (isNS1) is a ~250 kDa complex composed of NS1 dimer and ApoA1. Immunoaffinity-purified isNS1 migrated at ~250 kDa on Native-PAGE, and reducing SDS-PAGE revealed two major bands at 50 kDa (NS1) and 25 kDa (ApoA1). Label-free quantification LC-MS showed NS1 and ApoA1 accounted for >77% of total ion intensity in the elute and >88% in the 250 kDa band.
results.evaluation: Multiple complementary biochemical techniques (Native-PAGE, SDS-PAGE, western blot, LC-MS) consistently demonstrate that isNS1 is a ~250 kDa complex of NS1 and ApoA1 (C21, C23-C27). The LFQ data showing >77% combined intensity provides strong quantitative support (C25-C27). This represents a well-validated biochemical characterization.

results.result: CryoEM structural analysis of isNS1wt complexed with Ab56.2 or Fab56.2 revealed that NS1 dimer is semi-embedded on a spherical HDL particle through its hydrophobic surface. The HDL dimensions were measured at 82 Å by 65 Å, consistent with known HDL structures. AlphaFold2-predicted models of NS1 dimer and Fab56.2 fitted into the cryoEM map with correlation value of 0.75.
results.evaluation: While the cryoEM data shows NS1 dimer associated with HDL-like spherical density (C29, C32), the authors explicitly state the reconstructions are limited to low resolutions (C31). The 0.75 correlation for model fitting is modest, and the structural interpretation relies heavily on computational predictions rather than high-resolution experimental data. The claim of 'semi-embedded' conformation (C33) is an inference from low-resolution maps.

results.result: Crosslinking mass spectrometry identified 28 NS1:NS1 and 29 ApoA1:ApoA1 intramolecular crosslinks, plus 25 NS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks in isNS1wt. The NS1:ApoA1 interactions mapped primarily to the β-roll and wing domains of NS1 and helices 3, 4, 8, and 10 of ApoA1. Validation against structural models showed 85% of NS1:NS1, 76% of NS1:ApoA1, and 62% of ApoA1:ApoA1 crosslinks satisfied the <30 Å distance cutoff.
results.evaluation: The XL-MS data provides detailed molecular interaction mapping with good validation rates against structural models (C39, C41, C42). The lower validation rate for ApoA1:ApoA1 crosslinks (62%) is reasonably explained by the known flexibility of ApoA1 dimers (C43). The data converges with the cryoEM findings to support NS1-HDL interaction through specific domains.

results.result: The T164S mutant (isNS1ts) showed a significant population (53.7%) of free NS1ts dimers bound to Fab56.2, compared to only 3.5% free dimers in isNS1wt. Fewer crosslinks were identified between isNS1ts and ApoA1 compared to isNS1wt, suggesting the T164S mutation weakens NS1-HDL affinity.
results.evaluation: The cryoEM data clearly shows a major difference in the proportion of free vs HDL-bound NS1 between wild-type and mutant (C34 vs C30). The reduced crosslinks in isNS1ts corroborate this finding (C44). However, the mechanistic interpretation of 'weaker affinity' is an inference that would benefit from direct binding measurements.

results.result: Recombinant sNS1 (rsNS1) forms oligomers of dimers, tetramers, and hexamers when crosslinked alone, but does not form stable complexes with exogenously added human HDL. Only 1 out of 6 rsNS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks satisfied the 30 Å distance cutoff when mapped to the NS1:ApoA1 cryoEM model.
results.evaluation: The XL-MS data clearly distinguishes rsNS1 behavior from isNS1 (C45-C49). The smearing pattern on SDS-PAGE with HDL addition (C46) and the poor validation of rsNS1:ApoA1 crosslinks (C49, only 17% vs 76% for isNS1) strongly support that rsNS1 does not form the same complex as infection-derived sNS1. This is an important negative control.

results.result: Epitope mapping using peptide competition ELISA and HDX-MS identified residues 300-310 of NS1 as the primary binding site for Ab56.2. HDX-MS showed protection against deuterium exchange at residues 286-347 of the C-terminal β-ladder, with the most significant change at residues 300-310.
results.evaluation: Two independent methods (peptide competition ELISA and HDX-MS) converge on the same epitope region (C51, C53-C55). The HDX-MS data shows protection even at long labeling times (100 min), indicating stable binding (C54). The complementary approaches provide strong support for the epitope identification.

results.result: HDX-MS analysis of Fab56.2 revealed that all three CDRs of the heavy chain and CDRL2 of the light chain showed protection against deuterium exchange upon binding rsNS1c. CDRH3 showed the largest magnitude decrease, with the heavy chain serving as the primary anchor for NS1 binding.
results.evaluation: The HDX-MS data systematically maps the paratope with clear differential protection patterns (C56-C58). The spatial co-localization of protected regions forming the binding interface (C59) is well-supported by the data. This provides detailed molecular understanding of the antibody-antigen interaction.

results.result: sNS1 from DENV-infected mouse sera and a human patient forms similar complexes with ApoA1 as isNS1. Immunoaffinity-purified sNS1ts from mouse sera was detected at ~250 kDa by both anti-ApoA1 and anti-NS1 antibodies. In human patient serum, increasing anti-ApoA1 antibody resulted in corresponding increase in sNS1 detection, demonstrating specific association.
results.evaluation: While the mouse sera data shows co-detection of NS1 and ApoA1 at ~250 kDa (C60), and the human patient data shows dose-dependent co-immunoprecipitation (C61), both experiments are limited by low sample numbers (pooled mouse sera, n=1 human patient). The sequence similarity argument (C63-C65) supports plausibility but doesn't validate the in vivo complex. More patient samples and direct structural confirmation would strengthen this claim.

results.result: The data does not support the widely held hexameric model of sNS1 with a ~28 Å central channel filled with lipid. Instead, the findings confirm that infection-derived sNS1 exists as NS1 dimer(s) associated with HDL, requiring an exposed hydrophobic face incompatible with the hexamer model.
results.evaluation: The structural and biochemical data consistently show NS1 dimers associated with HDL rather than hexamers (C2, C20, C37-C41). The authors acknowledge their data confirms recent findings by Benfrid et al. 2022 (C72). The argument about lipid content and exposed hydrophobic surfaces (C74-C75) is logical given the HDL interaction data. However, the limitation to one antibody for purification (acknowledged in C71) means other NS1 populations cannot be ruled out.

results.result: Up to two NS1 dimers can dock onto a single HDL particle in infection-derived sNS1, similar to in vitro reconstitution studies. The concentration of isNS1:HDL (~30 μg/mL) is closer to clinically reported sNS1 concentrations (50 μg/mL) than the high concentrations (400 μg/mL) used in reconstitution studies, suggesting the NS1:HDL ratio varies with protein concentration.
results.evaluation: The cryoEM observations of up to two NS1 dimers per HDL (C68) are consistent with previous reconstitution studies (C67). The concentration comparison (C69) is valid and important for physiological relevance. The inference about concentration-dependent stoichiometry (C70) is reasonable but would benefit from systematic titration experiments.

results.result: Background on dengue virus, NS1 protein, and previous structural studies. DENV causes significant global health burden with severe infections characterized by endothelial dysfunction associated with sNS1. NS1 exists in multiple forms and has been structurally characterized, with previous models suggesting hexameric sNS1 and recent evidence of NS1-HDL interactions.
results.evaluation: These claims provide established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations (C5-C19). They set the context for the current study but do not represent new findings. The information is well-documented in the literature.

results.result: Previous functional studies showed isNS1 triggers proinflammatory cytokine production in human PBMCs, more pronounced with the T164S mutant. Provisional TEER assay data indicates acid-eluted isNS1 induces endothelial hyperpermeability. The authors propose that weaker HDL binding of the T164S mutant may explain increased disease severity through enhanced free sNS1 availability.
results.evaluation: The functional data is cited from previous work (C77-C78) rather than presented here. The TEER data is described as 'provisional' (C79), suggesting incomplete analysis. The mechanistic explanation (C81) is highly speculative, connecting structural observations to in vivo pathology without direct experimental validation. This represents a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated result.

results.result: Discussion of conflicting literature on NS1:HDL complex function. Some studies show sNS1:HDL triggers proinflammatory signals and interacts with SR-BI receptor, while others show ApoA1 neutralizes NS1 proinflammatory effects and exogenous NS1 fails to worsen vascular leakage in mice.
results.evaluation: These claims accurately summarize contradictory findings in the literature (C82-C92), all supported by appropriate citations. The authors acknowledge these discrepancies and call for physiologically relevant studies. This represents a fair assessment of the field's current state rather than new experimental findings.

results.result: The oligomeric state of NS1 is dynamic and may vary depending on context and environment.
results.evaluation: This is a reasonable speculation (C76) given the data showing different NS1 oligomeric states under different conditions (infection-derived vs recombinant, with/without HDL). However, it's a general statement rather than a specific finding.

results.result: The major species of infection-derived sNS1 (isNS1) is a complex of NS1 dimer partially embedded in an HDL particle composed of ApoA1, as determined by Native-PAGE, SDS-PAGE, mass spectrometry, and cryoEM showing ~250 kDa complexes with NS1 and ApoA1 as major components, with the NS1 dimer semi-embedded on HDL through its hydrophobic surface.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the NS1-HDL association is demonstrated but express serious concerns about the structural interpretation. Reviewer 2 states the cryoEM maps are 'of poor quality' with 'wildly overstated' resolutions, noting 'none of the figures are convincing that NS1, Ab56.2 or Fab56.2 are correctly fit into EM maps' and 'there is no indication of ApoA1 helices.' Reviewer 1 notes 'the electron density maps for their structures do appear to be a bit overfitted.' The Editor summarizes that 'the new claims in this study are unfortunately only inadequately supported by the methods and analyses used.'

results.result: Crosslinking mass spectrometry identified 28 NS1:NS1 and 29 ApoA1:ApoA1 intramolecular crosslinks, as well as 25 NS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks for isNS1wt, with NS1 residues involved in crosslinks located mainly on the β-roll and wing domains, and 76% of NS1:ApoA1 crosslinks satisfying the <30 Å distance cutoff when validated on the cryoEM model.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 acknowledges 'crosslinking-mass spec was used to detect contacts between NS1 and ApoA1, providing strong validation of the sNS1-HDL association' but critically notes 'as the crosslinks were detected in a bulk sample, they show that NS1 is near ApoA1 in many/most HDL particles, but they do not indicate a specific protein-protein complex. Thus, the data do not support the model of an NS1-ApoA1 complex in Fig 4d.' The reviewer also states 'a specific NS1-ApoA1 interaction should have evidence in the EM maps (helical density for ApoA1), but none is shown or mentioned.'

results.result: The isNS1ts (T164S mutant) showed a significant sub-population of free NS1ts dimer bound to two units of Fab56.2 (53.7%), with fewer crosslinks between isNS1ts and ApoA1 compared to isNS1wt, suggesting isNS1ts may have weaker affinity to HDL and is more dynamic in its association with host proteins than isNS1wt.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes 'for their mutant NS1-T164S, they find similar structures, but in contrast to NS1-WT, they visualize free NS1 dimers in complex with 2 Fabs (similar to what's been reported previously) as one of the major species. This highlights that different NS1 species have markedly divergent structural dynamics.' However, the overall structural quality concerns raised by reviewers cast doubt on the interpretation. The mechanistic speculation about weaker HDL binding is not directly validated.

results.result: The sNS1 in sera from DENV-infected mice and a human patient form a similar complex as isNS1, with mouse sera immunoaffinity purified sNS1ts detected at ~250 kDa by both anti-ApoA1 and anti-NS1 antibodies, and increasing anti-ApoA1 antibody for pull-down resulted in corresponding increase in sNS1 detected by ELISA in human patient serum.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes 'the authors find that NS1 isolated from DENV infected mice is also present as a >250 kD species containing ApoA1' and 'they further determine that immunoprecipitation of ApoA1 out of the sera from a single dengue patient correlates with levels of NS1 (presumably COIPed by ApoA1) in a dose-dependent manner.' However, both reviewers emphasize that the purification methodology using a single monoclonal antibody introduces significant bias, limiting conclusions about the native oligomeric state. Reviewer 1 states 'the overarching conclusion drawn by the authors, that the major species of NS1 in vivo is a dimer in complex with ApoA1, is not supported by the data in this study given the methodology of using a single monoclonal antibody.'

results.result: Recombinant sNS1 (rsNS1) alone appeared as higher oligomer bands of dimers, tetramers, and hexamers on SDS-PAGE, and when mixed with human HDL showed different crosslinking patterns than isNS1, with only one out of six rsNS1:ApoA1 intermolecular crosslinks within the 30 Å cutoff distance, suggesting rsNS1 may form oligomers of dimers but not a stable complex with HDL under the tested conditions.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 notes 'the finding that sNS1-ApoA1 crosslinks involved residues on the hydrophobic surface of the NS1 dimer confirms previous data that this NS1 surface engages with membranes and lipids.' However, the interpretation that rsNS1 does not form complexes with HDL is questioned by the overall methodological concerns. Reviewer 1 emphasizes that 'the oligomeric state of NS1 is dynamic and can shift depending on context and environment. This means that the methodology used for NS1 production and purification will strongly impact the results of a study.'

results.result: Peptide competition ELISA and HDX-MS identified the Ab56.2 epitope on NS1 at residues 316-330 (primary epitope at 300-310), with the paratope formed by CDRH1-3 and CDRL2 loops of Fab56.2, where the heavy chain serves as the primary anchor.
results.evaluation: These epitope mapping results using peptide competition ELISA and HDX-MS are not specifically critiqued by reviewers. The methods are standard and the claims about antibody binding sites are more straightforward than the structural interpretations. No reviewer raised concerns about these specific findings.

results.result: The data does not support the widely held view that sNS1 is composed of a trimer of NS1 dimers with a ~28 Å wide central channel filled with lipid, instead confirming observations that NS1 dimers associate with HDL, with the interaction requiring an exposed hydrophobic face of NS1 that is incompatible with the hexamer model.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 strongly challenges this conclusion, stating 'the Discussion reflects a view that the NS1 secreted from virus-infected cells is a 1:1 sNS1dimer:HDL complex with the specific NS1-ApoA1 contacts detected by crosslinking mass spec. This is inconsistent with both the neg-stain 2D class average with 2 sNS1 dimers on an HDL (Fig S1c) and with the recent study of Flamand & co-workers showing 1-3 NS1 dimers per HDL.' Reviewer 1 states 'the overarching conclusion drawn by the authors, that the major species of NS1 in vivo is a dimer in complex with ApoA1, is not supported by the data in this study given the methodology of using a single monoclonal antibody to immunoprecipitate NS1.' The Editor notes 'more rigorous approaches are needed to justify the main conclusion that the structure of the viral toxin derived from infected cells in this study is distinct from previously reported structures.'

results.result: Acid-eluted isNS1 proteins in this study induce endothelial hyperpermeability as shown by provisional TEER assay data with human umbilical vascular endothelial cells (hUVEC).
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly states 'the study does not provide any functional assays to demonstrate activity of their proteins' and 'the authors do not include controls to test functionality of their NS1 stocks (capacity to trigger endothelial dysfunction or immune cell activation).' Reviewer 2 notes 'the paper lacks any validation that the purified sNS1 retains established functions, for example the ability to enhance virus infectivity or to promote endothelial dysfunction.' The mention of 'provisional' TEER data suggests incomplete validation. Reviewer 1 further states in revised comments 'a critically important control that is missing from this study is to determine if the anti-NS1 mAb 56.2 prevents NS1 from interacting with cells, triggering the release of proinflammatory cytokines from immune cells, or mediating endothelial dysfunction.'

results.result: CryoEM structural analysis of isNS1 complexes with Ab56.2 and Fab56.2 showed NS1 dimer:HDL complexes with AlphaFold2 models fitted to maps with correlation value of 0.75, with observations of up to two NS1 dimers docked onto an HDL particle, and the concentration of isNS1:HDL (~30 μg/mL) being closer to clinically reported concentrations (50 μg/mL) than in vitro reconstitution studies.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 provides extensive criticism of the cryoEM structural quality: 'the cryoEM results are disappointing. The cryo 2D class averages and refined EM map in Fig S4 are of poor quality... The stated resolutions (3.42 & 3.82 Å) for the sNS1ts-Fab56.2 are wildly incompatible with the images of the refined maps... At those resolutions, clear secondary structural elements should be visible throughout the map.' The reviewer notes 'the samples were clearly challenging for cryoEM, leading to poor quality maps that were difficult to interpret.' Reviewer 2 also states 'the models for both structures are implausible due to a large steric clash of Fab56.2 and the end of the NS1. The Fab and NS1 protein backbones interpenetrate by nearly 20 Å.'

comparisons.comparison: Major disagreement on structural interpretation. OpenEval finds the biochemical characterization of NS1-HDL complex well-validated and SUPPORTED (C2, C20-C27). Peer reviewers acknowledge the NS1-HDL association but rate UNCERTAIN due to serious concerns about cryoEM map quality, overfitting, and lack of visible ApoA1 helical density (C29, C32, C33). Reviewer 2 states resolutions are 'wildly overstated' and maps are 'of poor quality.'

Both address cryoEM structural quality (C28, C30, C31). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN acknowledging low resolution and modest correlation, but accepts the data as informative. Peer reviewers are much more critical (UNCERTAIN), with Reviewer 2 stating maps are 'of poor quality,' resolutions 'wildly incompatible,' and noting 'large steric clash' with Fab interpenetrating NS1 by nearly 20 Å.

Significant disagreement on XL-MS interpretation (C3, C37-C43). OpenEval finds the crosslinking data SUPPORTED with good validation rates providing detailed molecular interaction mapping. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 acknowledging the data validates NS1-HDL association but critically noting 'crosslinks were detected in a bulk sample' and 'do not indicate a specific protein-protein complex,' thus not supporting the specific NS1-ApoA1 model.

Both address mutant NS1ts data (C34-C36, C44). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, finding clear differences between wild-type and mutant. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 noting the mutant findings but expressing that overall structural quality concerns and methodological limitations cast doubt on mechanistic interpretations.

Partial agreement on rsNS1 negative control (C45-C50). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, finding the data clearly distinguishes rsNS1 from isNS1. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the crosslink findings confirm NS1 hydrophobic surface engagement but questioning interpretation due to overall methodological concerns about NS1 oligomeric state dynamics.

Strong agreement on epitope mapping (C51-C55). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on convergence of peptide competition ELISA and HDX-MS. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, with no specific criticisms raised about these straightforward antibody binding site determinations using standard methods.

Agreement on paratope mapping (C56-C59). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for HDX-MS systematic mapping of antibody binding interface. This overlaps with peer R6 covering both epitope and paratope mapping (C51-C59), which peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED without specific concerns about the HDX-MS methodology.

Agreement on uncertainty of in vivo complex (C4, C60, C61, C66). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to low sample numbers and lack of direct structural confirmation. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 emphasizing that using a single monoclonal antibody for purification introduces significant bias, stating 'the overarching conclusion... is not supported by the data.'

Major disagreement on main conclusion about NS1 oligomeric state (C71-C75). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, accepting the dimer-HDL model while acknowledging purification limitations. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 stating the conclusion is 'inconsistent' with their own data showing 2 dimers per HDL, and Reviewer 1 stating the main conclusion 'is not supported by the data' due to single antibody methodology.

Both address stoichiometry observations (C68-C70). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, finding cryoEM observations of up to 2 NS1 dimers per HDL consistent with literature. This overlaps with peer R9's concerns about cryoEM quality and peer R7's criticism that the authors' 1:1 model contradicts their own data showing 2 dimers per HDL.

Agreement on uncertainty of functional validation (C79, C81). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting TEER data is 'provisional' and mechanistic explanations are speculative. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with both Reviewers 1 and 2 explicitly stating the study lacks functional assays to validate NS1 activity (endothelial dysfunction, immune cell activation).

OpenEval rates background/literature claims (C1, C5-C19) as SUPPORTED, noting they provide established context with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel experimental claims rather than background information.

OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for claims summarizing contradictory literature findings (C82-C92), noting fair assessment of field's current state. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent literature summary rather than new experimental findings.

OpenEval rates SUPPORTED for general speculation about NS1 oligomeric state context-dependence (C76). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific general statement, though peer reviewers extensively discuss oligomeric state issues in other contexts.
